cues.en: My name is Mike. By day I'm a tech leader of the account security team at Google and sometimes in my spare time I work on Bitcoin as well. So I'm one of the Bitcoin developers
cues.zh: 我叫Mike。白天我是Google账户安全团队的技术负责人，业余时间也会研究比特币。所以我是比特币开发者之一

cues.en: and I've been involved with Bitcoin since around April
cues.zh: 我从大约2009年4月就开始参与比特币了

cues.en: back when it was basically just me and Satoshi. And I left for a bit and came back. So today, I'm going talk to about the future of Bitcoin. And I'm not talking about the short term future, I'm talking about the long term future, the next five, ten years. If you want to know about the next six or twelve months, there's a talk tomorrow by Peter Will and also Jeff Garzik, and they will tell you about what's happening right now.
cues.zh: 那时候基本上只有我和中本聪。后来我离开了一段时间，又回来了。今天我要讲的是比特币的未来。我说的不是短期未来，而是长期未来，未来五到十年。如果你想知道未来六个月或十二个月的情况，明天Peter Will和Jeff Garzik会有一场演讲，他们会告诉你现在正在发生什么。

cues.en: But I want to explore the long term future because it's important that we build the case for cryptocurrencies
cues.zh: 但我想探讨长期未来，因为我们需要为比特币这样的加密货币建立论据，这很重要

cues.en: like Bitcoin. Today there's an idea, there's this meme that things like Bitcoin are useful only for buying drugs or maybe just as a cheaper way of doing what you can do with credit cards.
cues.zh: 如今有一种观点，一种迷因，认为比特币之类的东西只适合买毒品，或者只是一种比信用卡更便宜的支付方式。

cues.en: And it's actually possible to do a lot more than that.
cues.zh: 而实际上，它能做的事情远不止这些。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 那么

cues.en: typically what I'm going to tell you about today is contracts.
cues.zh: 今天我主要要跟大家讲的是合约。

cues.en: Now, these ideas aren't totally new. This quote is from Satoshi in 2010,
cues.zh: 这些想法并不完全新鲜。这句话出自中本聪2010年的话，

cues.en: and he said the design supports a tremendous variety of possible transaction types that I designed years ago. Escrow transactions, bonded contracts, third party arbitration, multi party signature, and so on. If Bitcoin catches on in a big way, these things we'll want to explore in the future, but they all had to be designed at the beginning to make sure they'd be possible later.
cues.zh: 他说，这个设计支持我多年前设计的极其多样的可能交易类型。托管交易、保证金合约、第三方仲裁、多方可签名等等。如果比特币大规模流行起来，这些是我们未来想要探索的东西，但它们必须在最初就设计好，以确保以后能够实现。

cues.en: Many people don't understand that Bitcoin's systems
cues.zh: 很多人不了解比特币系统中的那些

cues.en: features which lie dormant. They're not used today.
cues.zh: 休眠功能。它们今天并未被使用。

cues.en: And when I was reimplementing Bitcoin and Java a few years ago, I came across these features and I asked Satoshi what are they for.
cues.zh: 几年前我用 Java 重新实现比特币时，遇到了这些功能，便问中本聪它们是干什么用的。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 然后

cues.en: he responded by giving me some basic training in the design of what he calls contracts,
cues.zh: 他通过给我做了一些基础培训来回应，讲的是他所称的“合约”的设计，

cues.en: and then he vanished,
cues.zh: 然后他就消失了，

cues.en: so the rest I want to figure out, we have to figure it out ourselves.
cues.zh: 所以剩下的部分我想弄明白，就得靠我们自己了。

cues.en: But I think you'll agree that relative to the state of Bitcoin in early twenty ten, it has caught on in a big way, and that means now is the time to explore these ideas.
cues.zh: 但我想你们会同意，相对于 2010 年初比特币的状态，它已经大规模流行起来了，这意味着现在是探索这些理念的时候了。

cues.en: There's a lot to get through, so I'm going to move quickly. Hands up here if you would say you're somewhat familiar with Bitcoin, how it works?
cues.zh: 内容很多，所以我讲快一点。觉得自己对比特币及其运作方式 somewhat 熟悉的人，请举手？

cues.en: Most.
cues.zh: 大多数。

cues.en: Okay, that's good. So this is not going to be a very technical talk, but I want state
cues.zh: 好，不错。所以这不是一个很技术性的演讲，但我想声明

cues.en: now that everything in this talk is implementable today by anyone who is a capable programmer.
cues.zh: 本次演讲中的所有内容，今天任何有能力的程序员都可以实现。

cues.en: This is not a talk full of wishes or wouldn't it be great if? It's a talk full of things that we know exactly how to implement the blueprints on the wiki if you want to go ahead and do it. Microfamous. It's a hello world of Bitcoin apps. This is why I discovered that OpenOffice has chosen weird constantly. Okay. No problem.
cues.zh: 这不是一个充满愿望或“要是……该多好”的演讲。这是一个充满我们确切知道如何实现的东西的演讲，蓝图就在 wiki 上，如果你想去做的话。微支付（Microfamous）。它是比特币应用的 hello world。这就是为什么我发现 OpenOffice 选择了奇怪的 constantly。好，没问题。

cues.en: So, micropayments.
cues.zh: 那么，微支付。

cues.en: This is like the basics of a hello world of advanced payments. Bitcoin transactions are really cheap,
cues.zh: 这就像是高级支付 hello world 的基础。比特币交易非常便宜，

cues.en: but but they are not completely free. Right? Whenever you make a Bitcoin payment, you have to broadcast
cues.zh: 但它们并非完全免费。对吧？每当你进行比特币支付时，你必须向整个网络广播

cues.en: a message to the entire network and everyone taking part in the Bitcoin system has to do some calculations and verify it. What that means is that Bitcoin is full of defenses that stop people flooding the network with lots and lots of tiny payments. Now you can make a tiny payment to someone like once, right? But then you have to wait a little bit until you can do it again.
cues.zh: 一条消息，比特币系统中每个参与者都必须做一些计算并验证它。这意味着比特币充满了防御机制，阻止人们用大量微小支付淹没网络。现在你可以向某人做一次微小支付，对吧？但之后你得等一会儿才能再做一次。

cues.en: And this isn't always what you want.
cues.zh: 但这并不总是你想要的。

cues.en: Typically,
cues.zh: 通常来说，

cues.en: good uses for micropayments involve repeated billing for like a very
cues.zh: 微支付很适合用于类似

cues.en: metered service,
cues.zh: 按量计费的服务，

cues.en: and you can't really do that with Bitcoin today. Or can you? Actually, you can. But it's a bit of a weird solution. You use something called a micropayment channel, and this means that you choose who you're going to interact with, the payer and the payee, and you broadcast a transaction
cues.zh: 但现在的比特币很难做到这一点。真做不到吗？其实可以。不过方案有点奇葩。你可以使用所谓的微支付通道，也就是选定交易对象，即付款方和收款方，然后广播一笔交易，

cues.en: that sets up a certain amount of value, and it can be quite large, let's say, you know, a $100 or something. And then you negotiate
cues.zh: 用来锁定一定金额，这个金额可以相当大，比如100美元左右。接着你们再协商

cues.en: another set of transactions which don't have to be broadcast.
cues.zh: 另一批不需要广播的交易。

cues.en: And those transactions decide how much of that 100 bitcoins each party gets. So some of it comes back to you, and some of it goes to them. And you can update this transaction hundreds of times per second. Right? You can actually pay, you know, increment
cues.zh: 这些交易决定了双方各分得那100个比特币中的多少。一部分退还给你，一部分转给对方。而且这种交易每秒可以更新数百次。对吧？你实际上可以进行，你知道的，递增式

cues.en: little payments in very small quantities.
cues.zh: 极小金额的微额支付。

cues.en: For example,
cues.zh: 举个例子，

cues.en: you think about, you know, many of us here have come to London from other countries,
cues.zh: 想想看，我们现场很多人都是从其他国家来伦敦的，

cues.en: we are surrounded everywhere we walk in the city by high quality, high speed internet connectivity we cannot use because it is a Wi Fi hotspot that is locked.
cues.zh: 走在城里随处都有高质量的高速网络，我们却用不了，因为那些Wi-Fi热点都上了锁。

cues.en: And these hotspots are locked for two reasons. One is accountability.
cues.zh: 这些热点上锁有两个原因。一是责任问题。

cues.en: People don't want people downloading,
cues.zh: 大家不希望有人去下载，

cues.en: you know, illegal materials and other things through their IP address because then they'll get blamed for it. And the other problem is billing. Like, why should I give my internet connection to you for free?
cues.zh: 通过自己的IP地址下载非法材料之类的，免得自己替人背锅。另一个问题则是计费：凭什么我要让你免费蹭我的网？

cues.en: And the result is that we have to use our mobile carriers who then charge us an arm and a leg. Now, solving accountability is pretty easy. You can just have the hotspot say, I'll only relay encrypted traffic to one destination, right? So you effectively have to set up a VPN connection through them. And then they say, well, it's encrypted. I don't know what's going on. It's not my problem, right? Someone else takes responsibility for this traffic.
cues.zh: 结果就是，我们不得不使用移动运营商，然后被他们狠狠地宰一笔。现在，解决责任归属问题其实很简单。你只需让热点声明：我只会将加密流量转发到一个目的地，对吧？所以你实际上必须通过它们建立VPN连接。然后它们会说，嗯，流量是加密的，我不知道里面是什么，这不关我的事，对吧？由别人来为这些流量负责。

cues.en: And then billing, we can do this with a Bitcoin micropayment.
cues.zh: 至于计费，我们可以用比特币微支付来实现。

cues.en: So what this means is if you have a Wi Fi hotspot running this software,
cues.zh: 所以这意味着，如果你有一个运行这套软件的Wi-Fi热点，

cues.en: then you can solve all this, and you just run it, and it can be open to anyone.
cues.zh: 那你就能解决所有这些问题，只需运行它，就可以对任何人开放。

cues.en: And it can be so open that your phone can just roam onto it for no interaction at all. It doesn't have to ask you anything. It just connects to this hotspot, starts paying for it. The hotspot can't scam you because of the Bitcoin protocol. Right? You don't have to worry about connecting to a node that's going to rip you off. The worst case, you lose maybe a fraction of a cent. It's not a problem.
cues.zh: 而且可以开放到你的手机能直接漫游上去，完全不需要任何交互。它不用问你任何事，直接连上这个热点，开始付费。热点没法骗你，因为有比特币协议，对吧？你不用担连上一个会坑你的节点。最坏的情况，你也就损失不到一美分。这不是问题。

cues.en: Dispute mediation. A big problem we have today in Bitcoin is there's no chargebacks. That is a strength. It is a big strength, as we heard from Tony yesterday. But is it also a weakness because it means if a transaction goes wrong, you have no recourse. The merchant has your money and you have nothing. Right? Now,
cues.zh: 争议调解。如今比特币的一大问题是无法退款。这是优势，正如昨天Tony所说，这是一大优势。但它是否也是劣势呢？因为这意味着如果交易出了问题，你无计可施。商家拿了你的钱，你什么也没有。对吧？现在，

cues.en: you can solve this very easily today with no technology at all. You just find someone you trust and you send them the money, and you say please act as a dispute mediator for us.
cues.zh: 今天你完全可以不用任何技术，轻松解决这个问题。你只需找一个你信任的人，把钱发给他们，然后说请为我们担任争议调解人。

cues.en: But it is very difficult to trust someone to hold large sums of money, even if they're really great guys. And I want to I want to reinforce at this point that when I talk about trusting people,
cues.zh: 但要信任某个人来保管大笔资金是非常困难的，哪怕他们真的是很棒的人。我想在这里强调，当我说到信任他人时，

cues.en: I'm not talking about are they a nice guy or are they a bit of a scammer. Right? You can be an incredibly nice person, well meaning, lovely person, and then you get hacked and your reputation changes immediately because
cues.zh: 我说的不是他们人好不好，或者是不是有点骗子。对吧？你可能是个特别好的人，心地善良、讨人喜欢，然后你被黑了，你的名声立刻就变了，因为

cues.en: effectively your behavior is no longer what it should be. So you've got to trust a third party to not only hold large sums of money and not steal it, but also to not get hacked. And this is very hard, right? You want specialist dispute mediators,
cues.zh: 你的行为实际上已经不再符合应有的样子。所以你得信任第三方，不仅要保管大笔资金不偷走，还得不被黑客攻击。这非常难，对吧？你需要专业的纠纷调解人，

cues.en: people who, if you buy a Stradivarius violin, they're going to be a specialist in violins and they can tell the difference between, oh, I received a regular violin or I received a classic
cues.zh: 有些人，如果你买一把斯特拉迪瓦里小提琴，他们会是 violin 专家，能分辨出，哦，我收到的是普通小提琴还是经典小提琴

cues.en: expensive one. But you don't want to trust them to be computer security experts as well. Bitcoin has n of n transactions. It allows you to send money to three people and two of them have to agree. And in fact, two and three here are variables. You can set them to whatever you want. So, for example, I can send
cues.zh: 代价很高。但你也不希望指望他们同时还是计算机安全专家。比特币有 n of n 交易。它允许你向三个人转账，其中两人必须同意。事实上，这里的二和三都是变量。你可以把它们设成任意值。所以，举个例子，我可以发送

cues.en: some money
cues.zh: 一些钱

cues.en: to an output that says, I need to agree,
cues.zh: 到一个输出，表示我需要同意，

cues.en: and the merchant needs to agree, or to an output that has me, the merchant, and the dispute mediator. Right? So if there's no disputes, then me and the merchant agree and the merchant gets the money. But if there is a dispute, and the violin isn't really a Stradivarius violin, it's a fake, then the mediator
cues.zh: 而商家需要同意，或者输出中包含我、商家和争议调解人。对吧？所以如果没有争议，那么我和商家达成一致，商家拿到钱。但如果有争议，而且那把小提琴实际上不是斯特拉迪瓦里小提琴，而是赝品，那么调解人

cues.en: and I agree and I get the money. Or the mediator and the merchant agree and the merchant gets the money. But at no point can the mediator ever steal the money. Right? They can decide who gets it, but they can't actually take it for themselves. So this means that it's much easier to become a mediator,
cues.zh: 我和调解人同意，钱就归我；或者调解人和商家同意，钱就归商家。但调解人在任何情况下都卷不走这笔钱。对吧？他们可以决定钱归谁，但绝不可能据为己有。这就意味着成为调解人的门槛要低得多，

cues.en: and you can have real specialists and really good
cues.zh: 你可以拥有真正的专家，而且非常出色。

cues.en: forms of dispute mediation.
cues.zh: 争议调解的形式。

cues.en: Now, that's great, but we're still talking about people. And often, the most interesting things you can do with Bitcoin come when you don't take existing use cases and re implement them, but you
cues.zh: 这很棒，但我们现在讨论的还是人。而 Bitcoin 最有趣的应用，往往不是把现有用例重新实现一遍，而是

cues.en: scale things down. So you say, okay, we've got this automated system that's really efficient. What happens now if we make it, if we take it to the next level? Right? Take people out of the equation completely. So
cues.zh: 把规模缩小。也就是说，我们已经有了一个非常高效的自动化系统，那如果我们更进一步、把它推向下一个层次会怎样？对吧？把人完全排除在外。所以

cues.en: an oracle is a program that runs other programs and then decides
cues.zh: oracle 就是一个运行其他程序，然后根据输出结果

cues.en: what kind of transaction to sign based on the output. So if the dispute you can think of it as disputes if the condition on which you wish to control payment is
cues.zh: 决定签署什么样交易的程序。你可以把它理解为争议处理——如果你想控制的付款条件

cues.en: testable by a program,
cues.zh: 可以由程序来检验，

cues.en: then you can actually just people entirely. And this has a couple of advantages. One is it's cheaper, of course.
cues.zh: 那你就完全可以把人彻底去掉。这样做有几个好处，一个是成本更低，这不用说。

cues.en: And another is that it's actually possible, through the Oracle protocols, to
cues.zh: 另一个好处是，通过 oracle 协议，实际上可以

cues.en: repeatedly check that this program
cues.zh: 反复验证这个程序

cues.en: is going to behave and do what you expect without actually having to send money.
cues.zh: 会按你预期的方式运行，而不需要真的发送资金。

cues.en: Okay. So here's an example.
cues.zh: 好，来看一个例子。

cues.en: An old man is...
cues.zh: 有一位老人……

cues.en: Has got a lot of money, and he wants to give his
cues.zh: 他有很多钱，想给

cues.en: grandson an inheritance,
cues.zh: 孙子留一笔遗产，

cues.en: either on the grandson's eighteenth birthday or when the man dies, whichever comes first.
cues.zh: 要么在孙子十八岁生日时，要么在他本人去世时，以先到者为准。

cues.en: Now the eighteenth birthday condition is very easy because Bitcoin has a feature called lock times. You can create a transaction that sends money that doesn't become valid until a certain time. Right? So you set the lock times for the son's eighteenth birthday, give him the transaction on a USB stick, whatever,
cues.zh: 十八岁生日这个条件很容易实现，因为 Bitcoin 有一个叫锁定时间的特性。你可以创建一笔交易去发送资金，但要到某个特定时间才会生效。对吧？所以你把锁定时间设成孙子十八岁生日，把交易存到 U 盘上交给他，诸如此类，

cues.en: and that's done.
cues.zh: 这就搞定了。

cues.en: But the condition that he gets the money if you die, that's that's hard. Right? Bitcoin miners have no concept of who's alive and who's dead. What you can do instead
cues.zh: 但他死后就能拿到钱这个条件，这很难办。对吧？比特币矿工根本不知道谁活着谁死了。你能做的替代方案是

cues.en: is, for example, if you live in this place where the certificate of death registers is online, like the state of Missouri, for example, you can write a program that just checks this database.
cues.zh: 比如说，如果你住的地方死亡证明登记是在线的，比如密苏里州，你可以写个程序直接查这个数据库。

cues.en: And then if
cues.zh: 然后如果

cues.en: the man has really died, it can say to the Oracle, please sign for this transaction and release the money.
cues.zh: 那人真的死了，它就能对Oracle说，请为这笔交易签名并释放资金。

cues.en: Another example, maybe you want to buy insurance in case your website gets hacked. The program can
cues.zh: 另一个例子，也许你想买保险以防网站被黑。程序可以

cues.en: go and search Google. And if the malware warning appears, then it knows the site's been hacked. This is a useful thing because you can't really fake it, right? If your website is being appeared as blacklisted on Google, it's also been blacklisted in Firefox and Chrome and Safari.
cues.zh: 去搜Google。如果出现恶意软件警告，它就知道网站被黑了。这很有用，因为你没法造假，对吧？如果你的网站被Google列为黑名单，它在Firefox、Chrome和Safari里也会被拉黑。

cues.en: And that means you really don't want to try and do insurance fraud. It's really difficult to do that.
cues.zh: 这意味着你根本别想搞保险欺诈。那真的很难做到。

cues.en: Bets as well, you know, if you want to release money depending on the certain value of an exchange rate, or whether something happened, you know, because these programs can do anything on the Internet, right? For maybe you want to do a bet on a sports event or you want to bet on someone doing an amazing thing, you can express that bet as a search over news articles, right? You could do a search on Google News and if certain combinations of phrases appear, you know the bet has been successfully completed, right? So a lot things can actually be done in an automated way.
cues.zh: 赌注也一样，如果你想根据某个汇率值或某件事是否发生来释放资金，因为这些程序能在互联网上做任何事，对吧？也许你想对体育赛事下注，或者赌某人能做成了不起的事，你可以把这个赌注表达成对新闻文章的搜索，对吧？你可以在Google News上搜索，如果出现某些短语组合，你就知道赌注成功完成了，对吧？所以很多事情其实都能自动化完成。

cues.en: And the advantage: because you can submit bogus challenges from Oracle,
cues.zh: 好处是：因为你可以用Oracle提交虚假的挑战，

cues.en: there's no danger that the guy who runs this program
cues.zh: 所以运行这个程序的人不会有风险

cues.en: turns around and says, hey, that's a really huge amount of money you want to release. Why didn't you cut me in? Which is a danger whenever you have a lot of money at play. Someone might turn around and say, I'm not going to release the money unless you cut me in. But you can challenge an oracle over and over again with bogus, non existing transactions,
cues.zh: 转过身来说，嘿，你想释放的金额可真大啊。怎么没让我分一杯羹？每当有大量资金在运作时，这就是个风险。有人可能会转身说，除非你让我参与，否则我不会释放这笔钱。但你可以用虚假的、不存在的交易反复挑战一个Oracle，

cues.en: so they can't do that. They don't know which is fake and which is real.
cues.zh: 所以他们做不到。他们分不清哪个是假的，哪个是真的。
